claims: The Artemis II mission uses the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket stands 322 feet (98 meters) tall.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket is the most powerful operational rocket.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket generates 8.8 million pounds of thrust at liftoff.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket propels four astronauts in the Orion capsule around the Moon.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket's total height is 322 feet (approximately 32 stories).
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket's thrust is about 17% more powerful than the Apollo-era Saturn V.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket weighs 5.75 million pounds when fully fueled.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket has a 212-foot core stage.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket has two 177-foot solid rocket boosters.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket has the Orion capsule on top.
The Orion capsule offers 330 cubic feet of habitable volume.
The Orion capsule's habitable volume is approximately 50% larger than the Apollo command modules.
